Filed from the AS-112 review (qa-ruben, 2026-09-11) under M6: eight invented cascade routes to .roster-title that re-enable wrapping in a browser while T1 (test/roster-truncation.test.js) stays green at 606/604/0/2. None is used by style.css today (verified: 0 div/* subject rules declaring a watched property can match the title div; 0 @scope/@layer/@import; 0 true content: decls; 0 [class] or escaped selectors) — future hazards of the AS-45 shape (T1's English 'no later or stronger rule re-enables wrapping' is wider than its algorithm), same class as P6/P7/P10 were at the AS-74 merge. Each was appended to a scratch copy of style.css on the AS-112 branch (9d70ae6), applied-at-site asserted, whole suite run, restored, porcelain proven empty.

GROUP A — parsed, but targets() says false (class-literal subject match only; .roster-title is a div, app.js L506):
 A1 '#roster-list li.roster-row div { white-space: normal; }' — spec (1,2,1) beats (0,1,0) in a browser.
 A2 '#roster-list * { white-space: normal; }' — spec (1,0,0) beats (0,1,0).
 A3 '[class~="roster-title"] { white-space: normal; }' — same element, later order wins.
 A4 '.roster\-title { white-space: normal; }' — CSS escape resolves to the same class; later order wins.
GROUP B — never parsed (walk() ignores every non-flattened at-rule wholesale; a statement at-rule with no block is glued into the NEXT rule's prelude):
 B1 '@scope (#roster-list) { .roster-title { white-space: normal; } }' — 0 rules from it; Chrome 118+/Safari 17.4+/Firefox 128+ apply it.
 B2 '@import url("x.css");' followed by '.roster-title { white-space: normal; }' — prelude becomes '@import …;\n.roster-title', starts with @, both dropped; a browser drops the misplaced @import and applies the rule.
 B3 '@layer x { .roster-title { white-space: normal !important; } }' — layered !important beats unlayered !important; already a RECORDED omission (AS-74 plan §3, AS-112 plan §1) — listed for completeness, not new.
GROUP C — parseBlocks collapses:
 C1 '.roster-status::after { content: "{"; }' then '.roster-title { white-space: normal; }' — unbalanced brace inside a string; depth never returns to 0, parseBlocks returns 0 blocks for both, guard green. (Balanced '"{}"' DOES throw via the AS-112 nesting check — AS-112 plan §1.2's 'would also throw' holds only for the balanced case.)

Suggested shape (planner's call; all cheap, all in the same doctrine as AS-112's H6 — loud instead of silent): (1) parseBlocks throws when depth != 0 at EOF (C1); (2) walk() throws on any @-prelude that is neither FLATTENED_AT nor an explicit IGNORED list (@keyframes|@font-face), and on a prelude containing ';' (B1, B2; B3 becomes loud too); (3) targets() treats a subject compound that is '*' or 'div' as targeting the title (conservative — 0 such rules declare a watched property today, so it passes; A1, A2), and recognises '[class~=roster-title]' with or without quotes and the '\-' escape (A3, A4). Each fix names its falsifier as a numbered criterion (M4); the observed red sets are in the AS-112 review comment and scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-112/mutants.log. Not filed alongside: row.className= / setAttribute('class') in orgNodeItem — probed, survive by design (AS-112 §1), judged not task-worthy: neither idiom appears in orgNodeItem, and either would replace the class set and break the visible org-node-row styling.

== FINDINGS FIRST (M5) ==

Blocking findings: 0.

Findings outside the criteria list: 2 (N1, N2 — both routes past targets()/walk() that the eight listed routes do not cover; both sit inside §1.4's recorded exclusions, so neither blocks this task — but §1.4's characterisation of N1 as "conservative" is wrong and the record should say so).

N1 — a comma inside an attribute value is a SILENT route, not a conservative mis-score. walk() splits the prelude on `,` before anything is bracket-aware, so `[title="a,b"]` becomes the halves `[title="a` and `b"]`, and neither half targets (the attribute-strip regex needs a closing `]`; `b"]` is not empty/`*`/`div`).
  Falsifier 1 (subject; any order; even !important): `.roster-title { white-space: nowrap; }` + `[title="a,b"] { white-space: normal !important; }` → cascade() returns `nowrap by .roster-title` — GREEN. The title div carries `title=emp.title` (app.js:507), so `div[title*=","] { white-space: normal; }` is the same silent shape (probe N1c).
  Falsifier 2 (ancestor; order-dependent): `[data-x="a,b"] .roster-title { white-space: normal; }` placed BEFORE the base rule → the half `b"] .roster-title` is scored (0,1,0), ties the base, later order wins → `nowrap` (GREEN); a browser scores (0,2,0) and wraps. Control: the same rule without the comma (`[title="ab"] .roster-title`) reds correctly at (0,2,0) (probe P6d). Placed AFTER the base it reds, with the garbage selector `b"] .roster-title` in the message (P6b) — that is the only ordering §1.4 considered.
  §6 asked me to "confirm the direction of the error is conservative": I cannot; it is conservative only when the comma-valued rule comes after the base rule. 0 such selectors in style.css; fix shape is a bracket-aware `,` split in walk() (the lastCompound technique) — a follow-up task, not this one.

N2 — a namespace-prefixed subject is a silent route of the A1/A2 kind. `*|div { white-space: normal !important; }` and `#roster-list *|* { … }` → targets() false (the `|` survives (c)'s stripping so `rest` is `*|div`), guard GREEN; a browser applies `*|div` to every div, `@namespace` or not. `|div` (no-namespace) correctly does not match HTML elements, so the fix is to strip a leading `[-\w*]*\|` before the type/universal check, or to throw on `|`. 0 `|` in style.css; exotic; follow-up only.

Confirmed and NOT filed (plan §1.3/§1.4/§6 — I agree with the reasoning in each case):
- Comment opener inside a string (§1.4 residual): `.x::after { content: "/*"; }` … `.roster-title { white-space: normal; }` … `.y::after { content: "*/"; }` → GREEN and silent — the swallowed span carries balanced braces so C1/C2 never fire (P2a). The never-closed `/*` (P2c) and the balanced-in-one-declaration `"/* */"` (P2b) both red on the wrapping rule. The plan's own scoping stands (0 string-bearing `content:` declarations; the only quoted values in style.css are font-family names).
- `@FONT-FACE`, `@MEDIA`, `@-moz-keyframes` all throw (`unknown at-rule … @FONT-FACE`) — the lists are case-sensitive and vendor-explicit. Decision: not a finding. A throw naming the at-rule is loud, not a route; add `/i` or the vendor the day the stylesheet writes one. `@-webkit-keyframes` is ignored, 0 rules, no throw (P7f).
- `:where(.roster-title)`, `:is(.roster-title)`, `div:where(.roster-title)` → UNSCORABLE throws in walk() before targets() is asked (P4a–c). `:where()` zeroing specificity cannot be scored silently → adequately loud; no task.
- Custom-property indirection: `white-space: var(--ws)` reds as a value outside the allowed set whether `--ws` is declared on the subject or an ancestor (P5a/b); `white-space: inherit` reds too (P5c). Adequately covered — the declaration is on the subject, and the guard does not resolve.
- Known false positives red as predicted, naming the selector: `[hidden] { display: none; }` → `none by [hidden]`; `[class^="org-"] { display: flex; }` → `flex by [class^="org-"]` (P8a/b). Known false throws confirmed: `[title=";"]` trips the statement-at-rule check; `.md\:flex` trips `unsupported escape` (P8c/d).
- Depth check under a flattened at-rule: an unclosed inner block under `@media` is caught by the OUTER parseBlocks call, whose message names `@media (min-width: 1px)` as the unclosed block (P9a/b); the inner prelude is not named, which is acceptable — the enclosing at-rule is. The inner call's own checks are reachable: `@media (x) { .a { … } @import url(x); }` throws `trailing content without a block: @import url(x);` from the inner call (Q14).
- Ancestors not evaluated: `#nonexistent .roster-title` and `.roster-title *` both red T1 (P10a/b); `.roster-title span` stays green (P10c); H4's new control `.t span` → null (X1). H4 no longer claims `.t *` is not the element.
- `@supports` nesting `@media` and the reverse: one rule each, condition `@supports (display: grid) and @media (min-width: 1px)` / the reverse order, and red on a wrapping rule (P3a/b). `@media` nested INSIDE a style rule: the AS-112 nesting throw wins (`cannot score nested style rule … under: .roster-title`, P3c) — record.
- Selector list with an attribute member: `a, [class~="roster-title"]` targets via the second member (P6a) — conservative.
- Case/vendor on the subject: `DIV`, `Div:Hover`, `*::before`, `[CLASS~="roster-title"]`, `[class~="roster-title" i]` all targeting with the right specificity (P7a–e). `.ROSTER-TITLE` correctly NOT targeting — class selectors are case-sensitive in HTML (Q4).
- Combinators without spaces (`#r>div`, `#r+div`, `#r~div`), a newline as descendant combinator, and `:nth-child(2n+1)` (the `+` sits inside parens) all resolve the subject correctly (Q3/Q9/Q10). `:root` counts as targeting (pseudo-class-only subject; same conservatism as `[hidden]`; 0 in style.css) — note only. `{ white-space: normal; }` with an empty prelude is dropped silently, as a browser drops it (Q6). A `]` inside a subject attribute value (`[title="a]b"]`) reads as not-targeting — reachable only if an employee title contains `]`; recorded, not filed.
- Seams: `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the branch against master (8e68358) and against feat/AS-124-tail-prefix-confirm both return a tree with no conflict block; AS-124 touches apps/chat/README.md, server.js, test/stream.test.js, test/watcher-events.test.js only; AS-109 (already merged, 993a2a9) touched api.test.js only. Disjoint.

Inline fixes: none. Nothing in the diff is trivia-level wrong; the comments read accurately against the code.
